 Saudi Arabia issues safety warnings for Riyadh, other regions 
 The Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen are continuing cross-border strikes. 
 1:20 A man inspects damage at the site of an airstrike, reportedly carried out by Saudi Arabia, that targeted the Asr district of Yemen's Houthi-held capital Sanaa on Oct. 24, 2026. Mohammed Huwais/AFP via Getty Images By Kevin Shalvey , David Brennan , and Nadine El-Bawab Last Updated: October 25, 2026, 3:33 AM EDT Share Follow ABC News on Google Talks between the U.S. and Iran have stalled despite the two countries signing a memorandum of understanding in June, aimed at ending the war that began with joint American-Israeli strikes on the country in February.
 The two sides have continued to exchange strikes, though have not returned to the intense fighting seen in the early stages of the conflict. The U.S. says it is enforcing a naval blockade of the country's Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman ports, while Iran claims control over the strategic Strait of Hormuz and continues to claim attacks on shipping transiting the waterway.
 Meanwhile, intensified fighting between Saudi-backed Yemeni forces and Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen has seen the latter repeatedly attack Saudi military and oil infrastructure facilities.
 See the most recent developments below.
 Key Headlines
 Oct 25, 2026, 3:27 AM EDT Saudi Arabia issues safety warnings for Riyadh, other regions 
 Oct 23, 2026, 10:41 PM EDT Intel finds Iran has 'substantially increased' efforts to target US officials abroad 
 Here's how the news is developing. Oct 25, 2026, 3:27 AM EDT 
 Saudi Arabia issues safety warnings for Riyadh, other regions 
 Saudi Arabia's General Directorate of Civil Defense issued safety warnings on Sunday morning for the Riyadh, Khamis Mushait and Abha regions, amid ongoing cross-border attacks by the Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen.
 The directorate said that the danger had passed in all three regions shortly after the warnings were issued.
 Oct 23, 2026, 10:41 PM EDT 
 Intel finds Iran has 'substantially increased' efforts to target US officials abroad 
 The U.S. intelligence community has gathered information through various channels indicating that Iran has "substantially increased" efforts to target American officials abroad, according to a memo sent from Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
 "The lethal plotting efforts by the Iranians against U.S. citizens have reached advanced stages in both the Middle East and certain other countries," Clayton wrote.
 U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio looks on as he speaks with members of the media at the Taj Mahal Palace hotel in Mumbai, India, Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. Kylie Cooper/Pool Reuters via AP Clayton also said that senior members of Rubio's staff had been briefed on the matter and that he would make every effort to downgrade as much of the intelligence as possible so that it could be shared more widely within the State Department.
 A U.S. official confirmed the authenticity of the memo, which is unclassified and dated Oct. 23.
 "When it comes to our staffing at embassies, we constantly evaluate new information about the security environment," the official said. "The threat of Houthi attacks and of Iranian terror plots targeting U.S. officials are informing our decisions on staffing adjustments for embassies on restricted operating status in the region."
 The existence of the memo was first reported by Axios.
 -ABC News' Shannon Kingston 
 Oct 23, 2026, 4:36 PM EDT 
 Tanker hit by projectile near Oman, UKMTO says 
 A tanker reported being hit by an unknown projectile while transiting in the Strait of Hormuz Thursday afternoon local time, according to the UKMTO. 
 The tanker was able to continue its voyage to the next port of call, according to the UKMTO. 
 -ABC News' Desiree Adib 
 Oct 23, 2026, 12:07 PM EDT 
 Trump says there is more oil coming out of Strait of Hormuz now than there was a year ago 
 Asked about whether a the stalemate between the U.S. and Iran could continue for a year and if the U.S. is preparing for an extended conflict, President Donald Trump told reporters the U.S. "could end it very quickly."
 "Iran is a failing nation. We're taking all the oil out that we want," Trump told reporters on Wednesday. "Everybody is taking oil out. In fact, last week we took more oil out than we have ever taken it out even before the war."
 "They have no money, the question is do we want to finish it off or do we let it do we just want to let it wither because we're getting everything we want," Trump said. 
 Trump also pointed to Iran's rising inflation.
 "Iran is not able to do much now. And we could if we wanted to just take all of the oil, we could take the whole country, we could take all of the oil," Trump said.
